jersey._comment: THE era-dependent field. Not a single per-source verdict.
jersey.verdict: NOT usable as a discriminator before ~1935; the 1920 roster page has no jersey column at all
jersey._kind_correction_2026_09_04: Report 06 declared this per_era from a 4-team-per-season sample. The full census of 103 NFL seasons and 117,300 player-rows shows column PRESENCE is also a PER-PAGE property: eight seasons contain teams that lack the column while their contemporaries carry it. It is not an early-era phenomenon - Las Vegas lacks it in 2020.
jersey.no_season_lacks_it_entirely: In NFL 1922-2024 every season has at least one team carrying the column. `column_absent_entirely` applies to APFA-1920 only.

games_played._kind_correction_2026_09_04: Declared per_league from report 06's 4-team sample. The full sweep of 34 non-NFL league-seasons shows it swings by season WITHIN a league: WLAF 1991 96.3% -> 1992 16.1%, an 80-point collapse in consecutive seasons of the same league. USFL 1983 86.7% -> 1985 42.0%. UFL games_started 2009 90.2% -> 2012 4.9%. per_league is one level too coarse.

league_codes._why_this_is_top_level: A wrong league code loads the wrong sport SILENTLY - the page renders, teams parse, rows ingest. This is not a note in a report; it is the first thing an ingest must get right.

VERIFIED_with_rosters.APFA: American Professional Football Association, 1920-1921 - the NFL's own first two seasons
VERIFIED_with_rosters.AFL: American Football League, 1960-1969 ONLY - the fourth AFL

AFL3.resolves_to: the ARENA Football League - a DIFFERENT SPORT
AFL3.danger: A build reaching for 'the third AFL' (1940-41) gets arena football. The page renders normally and the rows parse, so nothing objects.
AFL3.verified: 2026-09-04, AFL3/1940 returns the title '1940 Arena Football League'
AFL3.rule: NEVER use AFL3. There is no StatsCrew code for the 1926, 1936-37 or 1940-41 AFLs.

AFL2.resolves_to: 1936 American Football League - the page EXISTS but carries NO roster links
AFL2.rule: the league-year page renders a title and lists nothing. Do not read an empty team list as an empty league.

NFLE.resolves_to: 1997 National Football League Europe - page exists, NO roster links

team_codes_are_globally_unique.verified: 2026-09-04 across 12 year-sharing league pairs (NFL/WFL 1974-75, NFL/USFL 1983-85, NFL/XFL 2020 and 2023, NFL/AFL 1960 and 1969, NFL/AAFC 1946, NFL/USFL2 2022, NFL/AAF 2019)
team_codes_are_globally_unique.consequence: a {TEAM}_{YEAR} cache key cannot merge two leagues' teams. Measured, not assumed - without the check the cache design was a hope.

leagues_the_brief_named_that_this_source: NFL Europe and its predecessors beyond WLAF 1991-92

cfl._measured: 2026-09-04, boundary probe of 1945/1979/2024/2025/2026 before the sweep

THE_SOURCE_BACK_MAPS_THE_LEAGUE_NAME.finding: Every year page 1945-1957 is titled 'Canadian Football League (CFL)' and every team code carries the CFL prefix. The CFL was not founded until 1958.
THE_SOURCE_BACK_MAPS_THE_LEAGUE_NAME.verified: page titles for 1945, 1950, 1954, 1957 all read 'Canadian Football League'; the strings Interprovincial / Big Four / IRFU / WIFU / Union appear NOWHERE on any of those pages
THE_SOURCE_BACK_MAPS_THE_LEAGUE_NAME.what_this_means: the pre-1958 league label is the SOURCE'S back-mapping, not an era-native fact. It is a claim attributed to StatsCrew, never an observed league identity.
THE_SOURCE_BACK_MAPS_THE_LEAGUE_NAME.what_we_did_NOT_do: we did not split 1945-57 into IRFU (east) and WIFU (west). That split is real but it is OUR knowledge, not this source's - assigning it here would be invention wearing a source's provenance, the exact failure the brief opens with.
THE_SOURCE_BACK_MAPS_THE_LEAGUE_NAME.open_gap: era-native league identity for 1945-1957 needs a source that actually states it.

1945.note: birth date at 33% is far below the previous worst measured anywhere (APFA 1920, 88.8%)

2026.note: IN-PROGRESS SEASON as of 2026-09-04. Excluded from the sweep: its GP values are a mid-season snapshot that would file indistinguishably from a final total, and the cache rule forbids re-fetching to correct them later.

sweep_result.years: 1945-2025 (2020 not played; 2026 in progress, held out)

cfl._where_the_predictions_live: field_availability.<field>.census_by_league_season, keyed CFL-<year>. An earlier draft put them in this block, which the ingest does not read - so every CFL season reported 'declaration makes NO prediction'. A declaration in the wrong place is not a declaration.

empty_roster_pages._what: teams a league-year page links but whose roster page parses to zero rows. They contribute nothing and, before this was measured, contributed it silently.

CFL-2020.finding: the league-year page renders but lists ZERO teams
CFL-2020.why: the CFL cancelled its 2020 season entirely (COVID-19). No games were played.
CFL-2020.how_it_surfaced: the ingest refused it - match rate 0.000 below the 0.95 floor - rather than recording an empty season as a successful one
CFL-2020.rule: a league-season with no teams is an ABSENCE to declare, not a sweep failure to retry. Retrying it would fetch the same empty page forever.

season_not_played._scope: any league. Keyed LEAGUE-YEAR. The ingest exits before fetching.

_documentation_only.known_conflicts: worked examples of conflicts already seen
_documentation_only.cfl: narrative of the CFL sweep; its enforceable parts moved to league_codes and season_not_played
_documentation_only._rule: keys addressed to a reader and to no code path. Everything NOT listed here must be read by something in src/ - see src/gate_declarations_are_read.py. This list living in the declaration rather than in the gate means widening it shows up in a diff.
_documentation_only.league_codes.team_codes_are_globally_uni: the measurement that makes R_{TEAM}_{YEAR} cache keys safe; the safety is in the key format, not a lookup
_documentation_only.league_codes.leagues_the_brief_named_tha: a negative result - leagues to seek elsewhere
_documentation_only._correction_2026_09_04: person_id_scheme was listed here as documentation. It was not: pattern {prefix}-{surname[:5]}{forename[:3]}{NNN} is a CONSTRAINT, and 36 stored slugs violated it, merging 46 men. It is now enforced by src/gate_slug_pattern.py. Marking a constraint 'documentation' is how a declaration stops being load-bearing without anyone editing it.
_documentation_only.stat_columns.PARSE_TRAP: how to parse, for a reader

stat_columns._why: A statistics table mixes COUNTED things with CALCULATED ones and formats them identically. Green Bay 1950 lists Tobin Rote with a passer Rating of 26.7 in the same row as his 224 attempts. The attempts were counted in 1950. The rating was computed by this source from a formula adopted in 1973 - nobody in 1950 knew it and no 1950 document states it.
stat_columns._rule: A column whose measure did not exist in the season it describes CANNOT be observed. It enters as source_derived or not at all. Enforced by src/gate_anachronism.py.

Rating.basis: GENERAL KNOWLEDGE, NOT YET CITED FROM A HELD SOURCE. The gate works off whatever year is declared here; if this year is wrong the gate is wrong, so it wants a citation before it is trusted as a fact.
Rating.measured_here: the column is PRESENT and POPULATED in 1950 - Tobin Rote 26.7, Paul Christman 49.2, 4 of 5 rows filled. Measured 2026-09-04.

Comp %.note: arithmetic on two counted columns. Derived in every era, including the ones that printed it.

PARSE_TRAP.symptom: a naive row regex returns ONLY the Totals line - reproduced 2026-09-04, '1 row' for Green Bay 1950
PARSE_TRAP.fix: chunk the <td> cells by header length
PARSE_TRAP.why_it_matters: it fails as a plausible small number, not as an error

stat_columns._generated: by src/declare_stat_columns.py from the cache, 2026-09-05. NOT hand-pasted: a hand-written census is how a conditional figure came to sit in a field read as absolute (report 22).
stat_columns._the_rule: PRESENCE is nearly constant across eras; FILL is what is era-native. Declare and check fill_by_decade. A check keyed on presence would call Tackle universal and be wrong in every season before 1980.
